summary.title: Getting the Interview Phone Screen Right
summary.one_liner: Learn how to run an effective software developer phone screen using five core question areas (coding, OO design, scripting/regexes, data structures, bits and bytes) to weed out weak candidates before in-person tests.
keywords: steve yegge five essential phone-screen questions
find phone numbers in html files
takeaways: Run the phone screen as an interviewer-led conversation rather than letting the candidate drive, and watch for one-trick ponies who know only one language.
Screen candidates on five areas: basic coding, OO design, scripting and regular expressions, common data structures, and bits and bytes.
Look for complete vacuums in an area rather than minor struggles; rustiness and need for hints are acceptable.
Good coding questions are simple, such as reversing a string, computing Fibonacci numbers, or printing odd numbers from 1 to 99.
Each candidate eliminated in the phone screen saves at least 8 man-hours that would otherwise be spent on a hands-on test.
summary.summary: Jeff Atwood responds to a reader's complaint that too many candidates pass the phone screen yet fail the face-to-face hands-on test. He summarizes Steve Yegge's "Five Essential Phone-Screen Questions" and gives example prompts for each area: simple coding, OO design, scripting and regexes (finding US phone numbers in 50,000 HTML files), data structures and big-O complexity, and bit manipulation. He stresses that interviewers should look for total vacuums in an area, not minor hesitation, and should ask how each failed candidate could have been filtered out earlier.
